name: Le Tandem L23 Rouge
summary: Light-bodied Loire red from Saumur-area vineyards; L23 indicates the 2023 vintage. Cabernet Franc brings structure and earthy spice while Grolleau contributes snappy red fruit and vibrant acidity. Notes include raspberry, sour cherry, cranberry, hibiscus or violet, and subtle pepper. Best lightly chilled with charcuterie, creamy salads, soft cheeses, mushrooms, light poultry, or grilled pork.

name: Lacrima Bianco
summary: Volcanic Campanian white from the slopes around Mount Somma and Vesuvius. The page describes an 80% Caprettone and 20% Catalanesca blend, with golden apple, yellow peach, white floral notes, flinty or smoky mineral presence, rounded texture, zesty citrus tension, and a long saline finish. Suggested pairings include grilled octopus, sea bass baked in salt, spaghetti alle vongole, zucchini flower pasta, provolone, and Caprese with buffalo mozzarella.

name: Bourgogne Blanc
summary: Classic white Burgundy from a Puligny-Montrachet family producer. Notes emphasize citrus, white florals, mineral character, crisp acidity, medium body, smooth texture, and subtle oak. Pair with seafood, roasted poultry, asparagus, mushroom risotto, soft cheeses, and butter or citrus sauces.

name: La Maison Blanche Sancerre Rouge
summary: Red Sancerre from Bue, with floral notes, cherry, raspberry, strawberry, blackberry, plum, earth, crushed rocks, pepper, oak spice, light to medium body, fresh acidity, and soft refined tannins. Pair with veal, poultry, game, salmon, tuna, mushroom risotto, charcuterie, and soft cheeses.

name: Martinolo Branco
summary: Distinctive Galician white from an 85% Godello and 15% Caino Blanco blend. The page notes clay, silt, pebbles, slate, and alluvium near the Sil River, spontaneous fermentation, 12 months in used French oak foudre, six months in stainless steel, white melon, textured mid-bodied fruit, vibrant minerality, saline edge, long slightly bitter finish, floral nuance, and sandalwood spice.

name: Barbarossa Rosso
summary: Biodynamic, minimal-intervention Veneto field blend associated with the Marcobarba project and Menti Winery. Notes include cherries, raspberries, strawberries, darker berries, earth, spice, cardamom, balsamic or herbaceous complexity, medium body, lively acidity, soft tannins, and slight-chill drinkability. Pair with grilled lamb, bean stews, pizza, cured meats, and semi-aged cheeses.

name: La Boheme
summary: Pays Nantais white from Melon de Bourgogne with a broader, creamier profile than typical Muscadet. Notes include cloudy straw color, white flowers, pear, green apple, mineral, buttery or honeyed undertones, succulent minerality, and vibrant acidity. Pair with oysters, shellfish, grilled or fried fish, garden salads, creamy clam chowder, and smoky bacon-accented dishes.

name: La Foret Gasselin Sancerre Rouge
summary: Fruit-forward red Sancerre with cherry, cherry core, crushed raspberry, juicy red plum, strawberry, violet, pepper, toast, cardamom, subtle spice, fresh plum, cassis, red raspberry, ripe almond, and a very subtle chocolate note. The page describes sustainable vineyard practices, Pinot Noir grown on clay-limestone soils, and pairings with grilled or roasted poultry, duck breast, pork tenderloin, salmon, charcuterie, soft cheeses, mushrooms, light pasta, and leaner burgers.

name: Detras Da Casa Larga Rias Baixas Blanco
summary: Rias Baixas white from 95% Albarino and 5% Treixadura, organically farmed in Condado do Tea on granitic sandy soils and fermented with indigenous yeasts. Described as fresh, creamy, mineral, slightly saline, and versatile with seafood, paella, creamy seafood pasta, grilled vegetables, poultry, lighter pork, cured meats, aged cheeses, fried chicken, and herbal or citrus salads.

name: Cuvee Carpe Diem
summary: Deeply colored 100% Alicante Bouschet with ripe blackberry, blackcurrant, plum, pepper, licorice, garrigue, earthy vegetal undertones, full body, powerful tannins, lively acidity, and intense dark fruit with spice and earth. Pair with steak, lamb, game, beef bourguignon, cassoulet, rosemary and thyme, olives, sun-dried tomatoes, strong aged cheeses, roasted root vegetables, or lentils.
